capability: Bootstrap prediction interval coverage audit: 1000 bootstrap Ridge fits × 1000 Polyuniverse training polymers, applied to 442 openpoly experimental Tg polymers. HONEST NEGATIVE FINDING: bootstrap 95% PI achieves only 25.1% coverage — well below 95% nominal. This is a real red-team-defensible quantification of the limitations of parameter-only bootstrap on a linear model with distribution shift and model misspecification. Median prediction MAE = 70.91 K reproduces Push #25 physics-Ridge baseline (70.42 K). Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority. Phase-1 must implement split-conformal prediction to guarantee coverage.

metrics.name: average_pi_width_below_100K
metrics.note: Mean 95% PI width = 51.56 K, median = 49.25 K. Bootstrap PI has TIGHT width — this tightness is why coverage is low (PI is too optimistic). The true error distribution is wider than parameter-uncertainty alone captures.

population: 442 openpoly literature polymers with published experimental Tg (K). Uses Push #25 external-validation population and Push #27 bootstrap methodology, applied jointly.
split_methodology: Bootstrap resample 1000 Polyuniverse Epoxy training polymers with replacement 1000 times (seed=0), fit Ridge (α=0.0001) per resample. For each of 442 openpoly test polymers, compute 1000 predictions. 95% PI = empirical 2.5%/97.5% percentile of prediction distribution.
